facts.raw_span: a small lump in his right hemiscrotum two months earlier during self-examination
no prior medical history
denied any history of scrotal trauma or inflammation
the lump’s size remained unchanged over two months
only mild discomfort during exercise, which resolved with rest
a painless, round, hazelnut-sized mass localized to the tail of the right epididymis
the testicles and groin were otherwise unremarkable
Scrotal ultrasonography demonstrated a solid, well-demarcated, hyperechoic, hypoperfused 1.3 × 1.1 cm mass at the tail of the right epididymis
containing two small hypoechoic foci, with no invasion of adjacent structures
Routine blood tests, coagulation profile, and serum tumor markers (AFP, LDH, CEA, and β-HCG) were all within normal limits
